question.knowledge_point: Applying the Second Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
question.problem:
Calculate
$\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}{\int }_{-5}^{x}(a{s}^{3}+b{s}^{2}+1)\,\text{d}s$
for $x>-5,$ where $a$ and $b$ are constants.
question.worked_solution:
The function $a{s}^{3}+b{s}^{2}+1$ is continuous on $[-5,x],$ where $x>-5.$ So, FTC II applies, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}{\int }_{-5}^{x}(a{s}^{3}+b{s}^{2}+1)\text{ }\,\text{d}t & =a{x}^{3}+b{x}^{2}+1.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
